speaker: Doctor
text: GREETING: I am Dr. Agent. You are presenting with double vision, difficulty climbing stairs, and upper limb weakness. To understand the urgency and nature of your condition, please describe when these symptoms first started and whether they worsen with exercise or rest.

speaker: Patient
text: The double vision usually happens when I look up or down, and the weakness in my arms and legs gets worse after activity but improves if I rest. I have not noticed balance problems or numbness.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Myasthenia Gravis.

The combination of diplopia that worsens with specific eye movements, proximal muscle weakness that fluctuates with activity, and the absence of sensory deficits or balance issues is highly characteristic of this condition. I am confident in this assessment based on the classic "fatigability" you described.
